sections.html:
Union County sits in the north Georgia mountains, about 90 miles from Atlanta, with Blairsville as the county seat. Brasstown Bald, the state's highest mountain, rises in the southeast corner. Mid-2025 estimates put the population at 27,859, up 13.1% from the 24,632 counted in 2020. Owners live in 84.4% of housing units, and the middle owner-occupied value is $307,400.

Sellers here hold very different properties: a mountain cabin, a lot in Blairsville, or acreage out in the county. Each needs its own pricing and access plan, and each needs a settled tax record before the deed changes hands. About 36.8% of residents are 65 or older, so estates of longtime owners are a common source of listings.

Acreage, mountain parcels and in-town lots are all assessed under the same 40% rule. The bill therefore depends mostly on land size, exemptions and any current-use covenant that comes with the parcel. Check which of those apply before you set a price.

Billing and valuing sit in different offices. The tax commissioner bills, collects and disburses taxes, while the assessors alone determine value. Start with the assessors if you question the value and with the tax commissioner if you question the amount owed.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 439-6017, at the courthouse, 65 Courthouse Street in Blairsville, for bills, payments and tag and title work.
  • Tax assessors: (706) 439-6011, open weekdays until half past four, for values, returns, homestead filings and exemptions.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds, including a copy of your warranty deed.

Union is unusual in one respect. The assessors, not the tax commissioner, take tax returns and homestead applications. The county has also hired an outside appraisal firm to help revalue residential, commercial, industrial and farm parcels, and field crews drive vehicles marked with a Union County seal. They stay outside homes and buildings.

Rate-setting is shared. The county commissioner sets the county levy, the Board of Education recommends the school rate, and Blairsville's governing body handles the city. The state revenue commissioner oversees the whole process, so a high bill is rarely about one office alone.

Real estate and business personal property tax is due December 20 each year. Mobile and modular home tax comes due on April 1, vehicle tax tracks the owner's birthday, and boats join the December 20 group once May notices have gone out. The county allows at least 60 days to pay the annual bill, and not getting a bill is no defense against owing it.

Once the deadline slips by, interest of 1% builds each month on the balance. Past 90 days, the office can record a tax lien, called a FIFA, at the Clerk of Superior Court, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Tax sale proceedings may start at the same 90-day mark.

Blairsville issues and collects its own city property tax, so city residents get a second bill from city hall.

Owners with wooded land should know that uncut timber escapes tax until it is sold or cut, and is then taxed on its full market value. On a single lump-sum timber sale, the purchaser sends the tax with form PT-283T to the tax commissioner inside five business days.

sections.h2: How does a Union County appeal work?
sections.html:
Notices of value go out in May, and the challenge period runs 45 days after the notice date. The first filing goes to the Board of Assessors. If no agreement follows, the file is forwarded to the Board of Equalization, which the Grand Jury appoints, and a further written notice to the assessors takes the case to Superior Court.

Arbitration or a certified hearing officer can replace the board for some owners, and that choice is made at filing. Mobile and modular home owners can contest twice, once at the return stage and again within 45 days after the bill goes out, usually in mid February.

Skipping a required return can draw a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest. Real estate returns run from January 1 to April 1 for property that changed hands or changed in value.

Bring a copy of your warranty deed to the assessors and file before April 1. The house must be yours and be where you live on January 1. Once approved, relief continues until you move, and a late application starts the following year.

Union's local homestead exemptions can be larger than the state's, so ask the assessors for current figures before you rely on any amount. Freeport covers business inventory. Current-use programs for farm and forest land demand a commitment to stay undeveloped, with stiff penalties for breaking it, so a buyer of acreage should ask whether a covenant is in place.

The county mails each year's bill to the person who owned the parcel at the start of January, so a buyer closing in March or September will not receive that year's statement. Arrange for the closing agent to pay it from your proceeds, and request a written payoff from the tax office a few days before closing.

A new owner gets no bill for the purchase year, so check any prorated payment on the settlement statement closely. For a mountain rental or a cabin left by a relative, ask about each year it was held and whether any FIFA is on file.

What to bring when you visit the courthouse: your warranty deed copy, the parcel number, and a photo ID. A cash sale can finish the payoff and the deed recording in a single courthouse visit, and it skips the repair requests a financed buyer's lender may raise.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
Start with the assessors. Confirm the parcel's value, ask whether a homestead exemption or a current-use covenant is on file, and find out whether any return is still owed for work you did on the property. Then call the tax commissioner and ask for the balance on each parcel you plan to sell, including any separate mobile home account.

Next, check the Clerk of Superior Court records for a FIFA against the property. If one is recorded, it must be paid in full before a buyer's title agent will clear it. Finally, tell your closing agent which office will issue the payoff letter, so the figure arrives before the closing date and not on the morning of it.

Estates deserve extra care, and so do mountain cabins used as rentals or second homes that sit empty for part of the year. Heirs often find that the bill was mailed to a relative who has died, and the notice never reached anyone. Ask the commissioner to confirm the mailing address on file and to list every open year before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: When must Union County property tax be paid?
faqs.a: By December 20 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and modular homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What does a late Union County payment cost?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 1% a month. A lien can follow once 90 days pass.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal a Union County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days counted from the notice date. The assessors see it first, then the equalization board.

faqs.q: Can I file a Union County homestead application late?
faqs.a: A late filing does not help the current year, but the assessors activate it for the next one.

faqs.q: Who collects Blairsville city property tax?
faqs.a: Blairsville bills its own portion. The county tax commissioner handles county and school bills.
